content.text: a plot of the degradation when running the test tool thusly:
java -jar target/test-ingester-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
http://localhost:8080/fedora/
fedoraAdmin fed 1000 500000
i.e. 1000 datatstreams with 500KB size each
a plot of the degradation when
updating
1000 datstreams

the same test with versionable and non versionable datastreams, and there seems to be a additional overhead which sems to add an additional linear factor during ingest. i'll retest this with 5000 datastreams to check if it stay linear..
didn't realize until i used a sufficently large data set that the time needed for the first update corresponds to the time needed for the last ingest.
so it seems to be just related to the FOXML size, which in turn speaks for an issue with the foxmldeserializer

SimpleDateFormat usage in DateUtility seems to be increasing, with a simple patch using a static instance of SimpleDateFormat the timings seem to be a bit better. I'll have to profile further into this..
might be related since the audit inline xml datastreams inflate the foxml size
the last test was done by commenting out the addition of the audit trail in DefaultManager and had the desired effect of mitigating the performance degradation greatly.
The datastream used has been set to be versionable.
Added statistics for the managed audit datastream update/ingest with plain audit datastreams and managed datastreams using attributes.
No further releases planned for 3.x
When adding a lot of manages datastreams to an object the ingestion throughput performance degrades in a linear fashion.
When e.g. ingesting 1000 managed datastreams with 500KB each the time needed for adding the datastream for the first is ~20ms and this degrades to ~130ms on a local installation.
I created a git hub project to reproduce this, which can be found here:
https://github.com/fasseg/fcrepo-test-ingester.git
which can be run as described in the README to reproduce this issue.
